default.evidence: Remake defaults: the section 6 table of docs/DEDICATED_SERVER_SCALING.md (30 Hz tick, 15 Hz near snapshots).

tribes.evidence: Tribes 1 and Tribes 2 (Torque/Darkstar) simulate in 32 ms ticks and send a state update per tick; the client predicts its own movement and the server corrects it (Torque TickMs = 32). 32 Hz stands in for 31.25 Hz. Units inside 100 m keep the per-tick update (the fight); the 100-400 m tier is 8 Hz and the far tier 4 Hz (it was 10.7 and 6.4): Torque's ghost priority already sends distant, unthreatening objects less often, and the clients interpolate over the gap. Saves a sixth of the records of a 64-player server.

es1.evidence: Earthsiege was a lockstep-style LAN game with no client prediction; the remake keeps the heavy, deliberate Herc feel by predicting only the pilot's own slow Herc and reconciling loosely (3 m).

starsiege.evidence: Starsiege (Dynamix, Darkstar, 1999) shares the Tribes engine family but its Hercs are as slow and heavy as Earthsiege's: kept at the es1 feel, hitscan lasers rewound.
